cards.hook: They invented state laws that never existed, ran the standard analysis, and found significant effects almost half the time.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Born in January, out of school weeks sooner
cards.hook: Two children, same street, same ability, born three months apart — and the law hands one of them less schooling.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Title said three months less schooling; the first stage is a few weeks, as the card rigor already said. Retitled.

cards.title: The best idea in econometrics was hiding in an appendix about butter
cards.hook: Fit a line through price and quantity and you get neither supply nor demand. The fix was printed in 1928, in an appendix, and ignored.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Ignored until the 1970s was wrong: IV was reinvented at the Cowles Commission in the 1940s, and Wright authorship was still disputed in 2003 (Stock-Trebbi).

cards.title: The lost planet that made least squares famous
cards.hook: A planet went missing in 1801. Getting it back made the tool every empirical paper still runs on famous — and started a priority war.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Title claimed least squares was invented for Ceres, but Gauss dated his use to 1795; retitled. Piazzi tracked Ceres 24 times in six weeks, not 41 nights.

cards.title: Remember orthogonal projection? That is all a regression is
cards.hook: Regression has no statistics in it. It is the nearest point in a subspace, and the residual is the perpendicular.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: How much your coefficient is lying, in two factors
cards.hook: You cannot measure ability. You can still work out which way it pushes your estimate, and usually that settles the argument.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: A model can predict you perfectly and lie about why
cards.hook: Regularisation makes an estimate biased on purpose. Omitted variables make it biased without asking. Only one of those has a dial.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Fixed effects is subtraction, and it throws away most of your data
cards.hook: You can delete a confounder you have never measured and cannot name — as long as it never changes.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Cuando el Sisbén aprendió dónde estaba la raya
cards.hook: El día en que los alcaldes conocieron la fórmula del Sisbén, la pobreza colombiana cambió de forma justo en el umbral.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Un punto en el Saber 11 y dos vidas distintas
cards.hook: Dos estudiantes separados por un punto en el Saber 11. Uno recibió beca completa y el otro no, y esa arbitrariedad es un experimento.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Author order fixed to Londono-Velez, Rodriguez y Sanchez per Crossref. Dropped the unverified 317/318 cutoff; the 56,5-86,5 % and 46 % figures match the abstract.

cards.title: Build the region where the policy never happened
cards.hook: One region, one policy, no control group. So they built a control group out of weighted pieces of other regions.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Two random walks look like soulmates
cards.hook: Generate two series with a coin flip each, regress one on the other, and the software will hand you a beautiful significant relationship.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Tulip mania is mostly a story about pamphlets
cards.hook: The founding legend of financial bubbles — ruined merchants, suicides, a nation gone mad over flowers — is mostly propaganda.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Remember martingales? That is what "efficient markets" means
cards.hook: Tomorrow's expected value is today's value. You met that as a fair game; finance calls it the efficient market hypothesis.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: The bet worth infinity that nobody would buy
cards.hook: A coin game worth infinite ducats in expectation, which nobody would pay twenty for. The fix became modern decision theory.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: The option price that ignores your opinion about the stock
cards.hook: The price of a bet on a stock rising does not depend on whether it is expected to rise. That is the result, not a simplification.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: The only free lunch in finance is a covariance term
cards.hook: Combine two risky assets and you can end up with less risk than either of them alone. The ingredient is correlation, not returns.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: The auction where telling the truth is a dominant strategy
cards.hook: Pay the second-highest bid and bidding your true value becomes optimal no matter what anyone else does.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Ganar la subasta es la primera mala noticia
cards.hook: Si ganó la subasta, su estimación era la más optimista de la sala. Eso casi nunca es una buena noticia.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

reviewed.notes: Corrected casi duplica: going from 3 to 20 bidders multiplies the required shading by about 1.65, not 2.

cards.title: Splitting a pie while every minute of arguing eats some of it
cards.hook: Nash wrote down four axioms and got one answer. Rubinstein modelled the haggling and got the same one.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: When nobody is sure what game they are actually in
cards.hook: Harsanyi's trick: if you do not know your opponent's payoffs, pretend nature dealt them, and the game becomes finite again.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Two honest Bayesians cannot knowingly disagree
cards.hook: If we start from the same prior and our probabilities are common knowledge, they must be equal. Not close. Equal.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Four aircraft, one runway, and exactly one fair bill
cards.hook: Four aircraft, one runway, one bill. There is exactly one split that satisfies a short list of fairness axioms.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: A two-page note that reorganised the social sciences
cards.hook: Two pages, one definition, one theorem — and economists have been saying "equilibrium" about things with no prices ever since.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Remember finite subcovers? That is why equilibria exist
cards.hook: Every existence theorem in economics is a compactness argument wearing a coat. Nash's is the cleanest one to undress.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: How aggressive should a population be? Exactly V over C.
cards.hook: The stable share of aggressive animals is the prize divided by the cost of the wound. Lizards in California run the experiment.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Remember natural selection? It was doing game theory
cards.hook: An evolutionarily stable strategy is a Nash equilibrium plus one extra inequality — and no rationality anywhere.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Chess was decided in 1913, in a way that helps nobody
cards.hook: Chess has a correct result under perfect play. It has had one since 1913, and nobody knows what it is.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Take the money on move one. Almost nobody does.
cards.hook: Backward induction says take the money and run on move one. Out of 662 games, that happened 37 times.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Chile reparte sus colegios con un algoritmo de 1962
cards.hook: Desde 2016 el cupo en un colegio chileno depende de un algoritmo de 1962 y de que usted diga la verdad.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: The algorithm that decides where American doctors work
cards.hook: Tens of thousands of American doctors are assigned to hospitals every March by a 1962 paper about marriage.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Any mechanism can be replaced by one where lying is pointless
cards.hook: Whatever your clever multi-stage procedure achieves, a form that people fill in honestly achieves the same thing.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: The game with no answer until you agree to be unpredictable
cards.hook: Your equilibrium mixture is not determined by your payoffs. It is determined by your opponent's.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Penalty kicks are the best experiment game theory ever got
cards.hook: More than 1,400 professional penalties, and both halves of von Neumann's minimax theorem survived the test.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: The trenches invented cooperation without meaning to
cards.hook: Two armies trying to kill each other stopped, without a word being exchanged, because they expected to meet again tomorrow.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Everything is an equilibrium, if the game never ends
cards.hook: Repetition explains cooperation. It also explains almost every other pattern of behaviour, which is the problem.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: A degree worth paying for even if it teaches you nothing
cards.hook: Spence's model assumes education adds nothing to productivity — and concludes that buying it is still rational.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: Remember Arrow's theorem? Here is what it actually forbids
cards.hook: "There is no perfect voting system" is not what Arrow proved, and the difference is where all the interesting work is.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: The equilibrium where you threaten what you would never do
cards.hook: "Enter my market and I will destroy us both" is a Nash equilibrium. That is a problem with Nash equilibrium.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: The prisoner's dilemma was invented to embarrass Nash
cards.hook: The most famous game in social science was invented to show that Nash equilibrium does not predict what people do.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: "Chess is not a game"
cards.hook: Von Neumann did not think chess was a game. He thought poker was.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: I am auctioning a dollar, and the runner-up pays too
cards.hook: I am auctioning a one-dollar bill. The winner pays their bid. So does the runner-up.
cards.author: author-econ-behavioral-1

cards.title: El profesor que rediseñó el Estado colombiano en unos meses
cards.hook: En 1923 Colombia no tenía banco central. Un profesor de Princeton llegó en marzo y se fue habiendo creado tres instituciones.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: "In the long run we are all dead"
cards.hook: The most quoted line in economics is usually deployed to mean the opposite of what Keynes was saying.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Prebisch, o por qué exportar café no alcanzaba
cards.hook: Ricardo decía que a cada quien le conviene especializarse. Prebisch miró cien años de precios y dijo: depende de en qué.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Three men, three countries, one idea, three years
cards.hook: In 1871 two men who had never heard of each other published the same idea in London and Vienna. A third followed in Lausanne.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Marx was a Ricardian, and the arithmetic caught up with him
cards.hook: Marx's economics starts from Ricardo's, taken seriously. The place it broke is an arithmetic problem that took a century to settle.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: The economics Nobel is not one of the Nobels
cards.hook: It was funded by a central bank for its own 300th birthday, seventy years after Alfred Nobel died.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: An invisible hand, twice, and never "the"
cards.hook: The most famous metaphor in economics appears twice in everything Adam Smith published, and never with the word 'the'.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Por qué el Banco de la República no le contesta al presidente
cards.hook: La Constitución de 1991 dice que el banco central no le presta plata al gobierno salvo por unanimidad. Esa frase tiene teoría detrás.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Eighteenth-century death rates, used to explain today's GDP
cards.hook: Where European settlers died they built extractive states; where they survived, institutions. That claim became an instrument.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Softened an unverifiable most-cited-paper superlative.

cards.title: A bank run is an equilibrium, not a panic
cards.hook: Queueing at a bank you believe is solvent is the rational move, provided you think everyone else will queue too.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Whether the debt explodes is one subtraction
cards.hook: Whether a public debt explodes or melts comes down to one subtraction, and the debt level is not in it.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: The man who built GDP put the warning in the same report
cards.hook: Congress asked him to invent a number for how the country was doing. He delivered it with a warning attached.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Kuznets quote restored verbatim: can, therefore, scarcely be inferred ... as defined above.

cards.title: El dólar que llegó a costar un millón
cards.hook: En agosto de 1985 un dólar costaba un millón de pesos bolivianos. Once días después de un decreto, los precios dejaron de subir.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Opening figures were wrong: 182,8 % is February 1985, not April 1984, and 2.177,2 % is in no Sachs table. Rebuilt on Sachs (1986), added as a source.

cards.title: Solow measured technology by measuring everything else
cards.hook: Subtract everything you can measure from growth. Whatever is left is technology — and in Solow's numbers, that was seven-eighths of it.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Remember phase lines? The whole Solow model is one
cards.hook: One state variable, one autonomous equation, one stable fixed point — and out falls a theory of why poor countries catch up.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Good news can push the unemployment rate up
cards.hook: A recovery can push the unemployment rate up, and it is not a statistical error. It is the definition doing its job.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Source title corrected to match the article it actually links to.

cards.title: The counterexample every textbook taught and nobody had found
cards.hook: For a century the textbook counterexample to downward-sloping demand had no confirmed example. Then someone ran the experiment in Hunan.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: The bees had contracts
cards.hook: The textbook example of a market failure turned out to have a going rate, printed in a pollination contract, for decades.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Cost falls by a fifth every time you double everything you have ever built
cards.hook: Airframe costs in 1936 fell by a fifth every time total production doubled. The same exponent turns up in ships, chips and solar panels.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: "Markets are efficient" is a theorem, and a much smaller one than it sounds
cards.hook: The theorem says a competitive equilibrium wastes nothing. It says nothing whatsoever about who gets what, and the proof shows why.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Remember Brouwer? It is why economists believe prices exist
cards.hook: Every market clearing at the same time is a fixed point of a continuous map on a simplex. That is not an analogy.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Three journals rejected the paper that won the Nobel
cards.hook: One referee rejected it as trivial. Another rejected it because, if it were right, nothing could ever be traded. It won a Nobel.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Two firms are enough to destroy a monopoly, on paper
cards.hook: With two firms setting prices, theory says the monopoly profit vanishes completely. Nobody believes it, and the reasons why are the field.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: Utility is a ranking with numbers glued on
cards.hook: Economists spent a century trying to measure pleasure, then realised the whole theory works if you only know what beats what.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

cards.title: El día que se rompió el pacto del café
cards.hook: El 4 de julio de 1989 se suspendieron las cuotas del café y el precio se partió por la mitad. Nadie tomó más tinto por eso.
cards.author: author-econ-metrics-1

reviewed.notes: Consejo Cafetero corrected to Consejo Internacional del Cafe. The 1,34 to 0,77 USD/lb indicator prices and the 4 July 1989 date check out.

cards.title: Athens thought elections were the aristocratic option
cards.hook: Classical Athens used elections only where it had to. The democratic method was the lottery.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Dated the kleroterion to the fourth century BCE, attributed the lot-vs-election reasoning to Aristotle (Politics 1294b) as received opinion, added that source, cross-linked the democracy series.

cards.title: Writing was invented to settle accounts
cards.hook: The oldest writing in the world is not a poem or a prayer. It is a list of how much barley somebody owed.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Schmandt-Besserat's token-to-writing reconstruction relabelled 'widely contested' rather than 'debated'.

cards.title: The plan that lost at Bretton Woods
cards.hook: Keynes went to Bretton Woods with a plan to punish surplus countries too. He lost, and the losing plan explains the next thirty years.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Triffin put the dilemma to Congress on 28 October 1959, not in 1960; Gold and the Dollar Crisis is the 1960 book. Dilemma heading re-dated.

cards.title: Remember what money is? Hungary, 1946, says it again
cards.hook: In Hungary in 1946 prices doubled about every fifteen hours. What is money, if it can do that?
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Callback opening now names hyperinflation. Sargent's four inflations dated to the 1920s (they exclude Hungary 1946). Unsourced street-sweeping detail replaced with the photographed one.

cards.title: Cómo se perdió Panamá
cards.hook: El Senado colombiano rechazó el tratado del canal en agosto de 1903 para negociar mejor. En noviembre ya no había nada que negociar.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Added exact Urrutia-Thomson dates (firmado 6 abr 1914, ratificado 20 abr 1921). Kept 'agosto de 1903' for the Senate rejection: sources split between 12 and 18 August.

cards.title: El día que Colombia cambió de hora y nadie se lo devolvió
cards.hook: En 1992 Colombia adelantó los relojes una hora para ahorrar luz. Fue la única vez que el país tuvo horario de verano.
cards.author: lead

cards.title: La una y cinco de la tarde, carrera séptima
cards.hook: Gaitán salía a almorzar. Le dispararon en plena carrera séptima y Bogotá ardió tres días.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Dropped the unsourced 'tres tiros'; added the Banrepcultural source that confirms 1:05 p.m.; death estimate tightened to 500-3.000.

cards.title: Una guerra sin nombre propio
cards.hook: Murieron alrededor de doscientas mil personas y el país nunca le puso un nombre propio: le dice La Violencia, como si fuera el clima.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: ¿Te acuerdas de los términos de intercambio? Prebisch los volvió política
cards.hook: Si exportas café e importas maquinaria, y el café se abarata frente a la maquinaria, trabajas más cada año por lo mismo.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: 'una razon inocente' changed to 'un cociente inocente' (razon reads ambiguously in Spanish).

cards.title: «Una sola nación con un solo vínculo»
cards.hook: Derrotado y sin ejército, en Kingston, Bolívar escribe la idea más ambiciosa del continente y explica por qué no va a ocurrir.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: El 20 de julio no fue lo que celebramos
cards.hook: El 20 de julio de 1810 Santa Fe no declaró la independencia. Juró lealtad a Fernando VII.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Removed the unverified attribution of the florero request to Luis de Rubio; the cited source names Santamaria and the Morales brothers.

cards.title: Dos hombres, dos ideas de país
cards.hook: El héroe y su vicepresidente se volvieron enemigos por una pregunta que Colombia todavía no cierra: cuánto poder debe tener el ejecutivo.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: El Dorado era una persona, no un lugar
cards.hook: El Dorado no era una ciudad ni un reino. Era un hombre cubierto de polvo de oro, una vez, en una laguna.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Remember that contagion follows edges, not distance?
cards.hook: Remember that epidemics spread along networks, not across maps? Here is the fourteenth century proving it.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Corrected the 1347-48 chronology (Genoa/Marseille that winter, Tunis by April 1348). The Caffa catapult story is uncorroborated (de' Mussi, not an eyewitness), not 'treated with caution'.

cards.title: The wages that would not stay down
cards.hook: The clearest evidence that wages rose after the plague is the law passed to stop them.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: England 7m to 2m was wrong (Broadberry: 4.8m in 1348 to 2.1m in 1400). 'Nominal wages doubled 1350-1450' was false (Clark: +19%) - rigor rebuilt on Clark and Munro. 1381 trigger fixed.

cards.title: The message never got tired, only the horses did
cards.hook: The Mongol post moved at the speed of a fresh horse, never a tired one.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Spacing and speed were misattributed: ~25 miles and 200-250 miles a day are Marco Polo's figures, not 'the chroniclers''. Polo added as a source; diagram and recall relabelled.

cards.title: A trucker got bored waiting at the docks
cards.hook: The single object that did most for globalisation is a corrugated steel box with no moving parts.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Levinson's figures are $5.83 a ton against 15.8 cents, not $5.86 and 16 cents; corrected in body and recall. McLean's dock epiphany labelled possibly apocryphal, as Levinson does.

cards.title: The first thing that ever went viral
cards.hook: Luther was not the first to attack indulgences. He was the first to do it where there was a printing press.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Melanchthon's account dated to 1546 and flagged as second-hand (he reached Wittenberg in 1518). Rubin's result quoted as 'at minimum' 29 points, the abstract's wording.

cards.title: There was no such thing, and this is a book about it
cards.hook: The best-known book on the Scientific Revolution opens by denying that it happened.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Quote confirmed verbatim. The publisher page serves the second edition, so the source now names it; the body keeps 1996 for the first.

cards.title: The metre is 0.2 millimetres wrong, and he knew
cards.hook: It was meant to be one ten-millionth of the pole-to-equator distance. It is 0.2 mm off, and the man who knew never said.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Arcs corrected: Delambre took Dunkirk-Rodez, Mechain Rodez-Barcelona. Cause of death softened to 'a fever, usually identified as yellow fever'. The 0.197 mm and its cause verified as written.

cards.title: The coincidence that was worth a Fields Medal
cards.hook: 196884 = 196883 + 1. Conway's word for the observation was moonshine, meaning nonsense. It took a Fields Medal to settle.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: The theorem no single person has read
cards.hook: Tens of thousands of pages, about a hundred authors, and an announcement in 1983 that turned out to be premature by twenty-one years.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Por qué un código QR sobrevive a que le tapen una esquina
cards.hook: Tape con el pulgar una esquina de un código QR y sigue funcionando. La razón es aritmética en un cuerpo de 256 elementos.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: The minimum-distance argument was wrong; rewrote it in the evaluation form and noted that the QR encoder uses the equivalent cyclic form.

cards.title: The Greek problems died in 1837 and nobody noticed
cards.hook: Two thousand years of failed constructions, settled by one observation: compasses only ever hand you square roots.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: There is no field with six elements, and there never will be
cards.hook: Not 6, not 10, not 12. Finite fields exist only at prime powers, and for each one there is exactly a single field.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Fields on the left, groups on the right, and a perfect mirror
cards.hook: Two lattices that look nothing alike turn out to be the same lattice, upside down. That is the whole of Galois theory.

series.title: Why you can't solve the quintic

cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Galois did not write it all the night before the duel
cards.hook: The duel was real, the letter was real. The boy inventing group theory overnight was assembled by biographers a century later.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Rothman 1982 verified via Crossref: Amer. Math. Monthly 89(2), 84-106. Added to the source title; linked the quote card.

cards.title: What Galois asked for, the night before the duel
cards.hook: The last request Galois made about his mathematics was not that anyone believe it.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Quote verified against the French original on fr.wikipedia; linked to the myth-busting story card.

cards.title: One group refuses to come apart, and that is the whole answer
cards.hook: There is no quintic formula because one 60-element group has no normal subgroups. That is the entire reason.

series.title: Why you can't solve the quintic

cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Run Galois theory backwards and nobody knows the answer
cards.hook: Every finite group should be the symmetry group of some rational equation. Nobody can prove it, but the last sporadic holdout fell in 2026.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: arXiv:2608.08538 fetched: Huang, Jackson, Lee, Poonen, Pries, Zhang, 9 Aug 2026, explicit degree-23 polynomial. Claim stands.

cards.title: Remember orbits? That is how you count necklaces
cards.hook: You cannot divide 64 colourings by 6 rotations. Average the fixed points instead and the answer comes out exactly.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: These are necklaces, not bracelets — 14 counts rotations only. Added the dihedral average (13) so the words match the group.

cards.title: The best thing a group can act on is itself
cards.hook: A p-group can never be entirely non-commutative. Its centre is always bigger than the identity, and conjugation is why.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Los diecisiete grupos del plano y la cuenta que nadie cierra
cards.hook: Solo hay diecisiete maneras de repetir un patrón hasta llenar el plano. Cuántas hay en la Alhambra es una pelea abierta.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: All four counts (Muller 12, the 14 misreading, Montesinos 17, Grunbaum 13) verified against Grunbaum 2006.

cards.title: The group stops being a list and starts doing something
cards.hook: Orbit times stabiliser equals the size of the group — and the proof is the coset tiling from last episode, reused without a single change.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Remember group actions? A string quartet is one
cards.hook: Transpose and invert a melody and you are using the symmetries of a 12-gon. A second copy of that group is hiding in the chords.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Corrected the duality statement (centraliser of a simply transitive action), the point stabilisers, and the overreach of the Schoenberg line.

cards.title: You are checking twice as many axioms as you need
cards.hook: Ask only for a left identity and left inverses. The right-handed versions arrive free — but mix the sides and it collapses.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: A symmetry is not a shape. It is a move.
cards.hook: A square has eight symmetries. Counting them is easy. Noticing that they form a system is the whole subject.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Energy is conserved because time has a symmetry, and only then
cards.hook: Energy conservation is not a law of nature. It is a consequence of the fact that the laws are the same today as yesterday.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Swing example changed to pumping so the body matches the time-dependent Lagrangian in the rigor.

cards.title: A published number that stayed wrong for twenty years
cards.hook: There are 49,487,367,289 groups of order 1024. For twenty years the published figure was off by 1,867.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Both figures verified (Burrell 2021, Comm. Algebra 50(6)); dropped the unverifiable account of how the 2001 miscount happened.

cards.title: The sentence Weyl chose to open with
cards.hook: Weyl opened his book on symmetry by admitting that the mathematical meaning is a choice, not the only one.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Quote checked against MacTutor's transcription (added as a source); restored the comma before 'and perfection'.

cards.title: Quotients are forgetting, on purpose
cards.hook: A clock forgets multiples of twelve on purpose. Normal subgroups are exactly the things a group is allowed to forget.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Groups have prime factorisation, and it is not enough
cards.hook: Groups factor into simple pieces, and the factorisation is unique. Unlike with integers, the pieces do not determine the group.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: An answer about one symmetry group that fills 60 gigabytes
cards.hook: The answer to one question about one exceptional Lie group is a 453,060-square matrix of polynomials.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Turn all the way around and you are not back where you started
cards.hook: Rotate a glass of water through 360 degrees and your arm is twisted. Through 720 and it is not. The group of rotations is the reason.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Serre asked a question and spent twenty years objecting to its name
cards.hook: Is every vector bundle over affine space trivial? Serre asked it in a footnote in 1955 and it took twenty-one years.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Two theorems from two different courses, proved once
cards.hook: Finite abelian groups and the Jordan form are the same theorem. You just feed it a different ring.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Rewrote the definition-first opening to lead with the two-courses-one-proof hook; linked the Jordan-form card.

cards.title: Six pages, self-printed, because he was paying
cards.hook: Abel cut his proof to six pages because he was paying the printer. The idea inside it moved the question from formulas to permutations.

series.title: Why you can't solve the quintic

cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: "Even permutation" is a theorem, not a convention
cards.hook: The same shuffle is 3 swaps or 17, your choice. Whether the count is odd or even is not your choice, and proving that takes a polynomial.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Remember groups? You have had one in a drawer since childhood
cards.hook: Reassemble a cube at random and only one arrangement in twelve is solvable. That factor of 12 is three conservation laws.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Callback retargeted to niche.games.puzzles; chess-go was the wrong node. Cube order, factorisation and God's number verified.

cards.title: The thousand-dollar prize for a position that does not exist
cards.hook: Loyd offered a thousand dollars for a puzzle position. Two mathematicians had already proved it unreachable — the year before the craze.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: A formula worth swearing an oath over, and then breaking it
cards.hook: A formula for the cubic was a weapon you kept secret. Cardano swore an oath to keep one, and then published it.

series.title: Why you can't solve the quintic

cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: 1545 to Ruffini is 254 years, not 275. Tartaglia, del Ferro, Fior and Ferrari all check out.

cards.title: Complex numbers did not come from $x^2=-1$
cards.hook: Three real roots, and Cardano's formula forces you through the square root of a negative number. Not clumsiness — a theorem.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: The theorem that had to go through the complex numbers
cards.hook: A statement purely about finite groups that nobody could prove without complex matrices — for sixty-eight years.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Goldschmidt and Bender split the proof by the order of the group, not by the parity of the prime.

cards.title: Two different groups with the same character table
cards.hook: The character table knows the order, the normal subgroups, whether the group is solvable. It does not know the group.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: The word "ideal" means "imaginary", and it always did
cards.hook: In one ring away from the integers, 6 factors two different ways. Ideals were invented to put the missing primes back.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Emmy Noether y la cadena que tiene que detenerse
cards.hook: Noether cambió el álgebra con una sola hipótesis: que ninguna cadena creciente de ideales pueda seguir para siempre.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Noether drew no salary until 1922, not a year after her 1919 habilitation. The Hilbert bathhouse line was already flagged as undocumented.

cards.title: A point is the set of functions that vanish on it
cards.hook: Throw away the points of a curve and keep only its ring of functions. The points come back as ideals, and you get extra ones for free.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: The one divisor that never lets you down
cards.hook: Lagrange's converse is false — except at primes, where it is true, and the proof fits on a napkin.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: A subgroup can never be an awkward size
cards.hook: A subgroup tiles its group: identical blocks, no overlaps, nothing left over. That one picture is Lagrange's theorem.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Fixed two errors: the cube has 24 rotations inside 48 symmetries, and a group of prime order does have the trivial subgroup.

cards.title: Fermat's little theorem is Lagrange's theorem in disguise
cards.hook: Fermat's little theorem is not a fact about primes. It is Lagrange's theorem applied to a group that happens to have p-1 elements.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: There is only one group of order 15. Prove it in four lines.
cards.hook: Order 8 gives you five different groups. Order 15 gives exactly one, and no cleverness will produce a second.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: A subgroup that nobody built
cards.hook: Wielandt proved that Sylow subgroups exist without constructing one. He counted subsets and let the arithmetic hand him a subgroup.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: How to find a subgroup you have no reason to believe exists
cards.hook: Lagrange's converse fails in general. Sylow found exactly where it survives — at the full prime powers — and turned it into a machine.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Chaos is a machine that reads the next binary digit
cards.hook: Strip chaos down to its simplest example and it is a machine that deletes the first binary digit of a number and shifts the rest left.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Fixed: periodic points are the purely periodic binary expansions (rationals with odd denominator); the eventually periodic ones are all the rationals.

cards.title: The forecast that changed because of three decimal places
cards.hook: In 1961 a weather simulation was restarted from a printout. Three missing decimal places produced a completely different season.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Why chaos does not win everywhere
cards.hook: Poincaré showed a nudge can wreck an orbit. Kolmogorov showed which ones survive: those with the most irrational frequencies.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: A complete space keeps the limits it promises
cards.hook: A Cauchy sequence is one that looks like it converges. Completeness is the promise that looking like it is enough.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Cross-linked to the metric-ruler card, which shares the C[0,1] example.

cards.title: Fold the map, and one point stays where it is
cards.hook: Drop a map of Bogota on the floor in Bogota. Exactly one point of the paper lies directly above the place it represents.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Picard-Lindelof: the Lipschitz constant is now uniform in t, and the local version (invariant ball, h below b/max|f|) that the statement skipped has been added.

cards.title: The monster is the typical case
cards.hook: Weierstrass's monster is not the exception. In the space of continuous functions almost every function is one.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: One complex derivative buys you all of them
cards.hook: On the real line, one derivative buys you almost nothing. In the complex plane, one derivative buys you all of them, plus a Taylor series.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Every polynomial has a root, and algebra cannot prove it
cards.hook: The fundamental theorem of algebra has no purely algebraic proof. The shortest one takes three lines and is entirely about analysis.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: 'the previous card' replaced by naming the idea, since the engine does not guarantee feed order.

cards.title: The proof nobody read for fifty years
cards.hook: The first proof that continuity implies the intermediate value theorem was published in 1817 in Prague, and then ignored for fifty years.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The function that breaks exactly where you can name it
cards.hook: There is a function continuous at every irrational and broken at every rational. The mirror image is impossible, and the reason is deep.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Derivatives can be wild, but they cannot jump
cards.hook: A derivative can be discontinuous at uncountably many points. It can still never have a jump. Nobody expects that combination.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Logic sometimes breeds monsters
cards.hook: Poincaré on the functions Weierstrass unleashed: monsters, invented to show the ancestors wrong.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Quote verified verbatim; page 125 could not be confirmed, so the citation now reads Science et Methode (1908) book II ch. 2 in Maitland's 1914 translation, with Wikiquote added as source.

cards.title: The curve with no direction, anywhere
cards.hook: In 1872 Weierstrass exhibited a curve you can draw without lifting the pen and that has a tangent at no point at all.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: La pregunta que un ingeniero guardó treinta años
cards.hook: Un ingeniero de YPF se hizo una pregunta en 1947 y la publicó en 1980. Hoy es la base matemática de un método de diagnóstico.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The corner that was not allowed to exist
cards.hook: Fourier claimed smooth waves could add up to a corner. The greatest analyst alive told him it was impossible, and blocked the paper.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Remember that a short pulse needs many frequencies?
cards.hook: Heisenberg's uncertainty principle is a theorem about Fourier transforms. The physics only supplies the exchange rate.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The conjecture everyone was trying to demolish
cards.hook: Everyone expected the counterexample. Carleson spent years hunting one, failed, and in 1966 proved the theorem instead.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The overshoot that refuses to shrink
cards.hook: Add a thousand terms to the Fourier series of a square wave and the little spike near the jump is still exactly 8.95% too tall.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Dirichlet kernel: the log N growth is the Lebesgue constant, not the total variation. Also fixed a distractor: 1.1790 is the peak for the plus/minus 1 square wave, not a unit jump.

cards.title: Pythagoras still works when the triangle has infinite sides
cards.hook: Fourier coefficients are not a trick. They are coordinates, computed the way you have always computed coordinates: project.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The unit ball loses compactness, then buys it back
cards.hook: In infinite dimensions, bounded sequences can refuse to have convergent subsequences. The repair is to change what convergence means.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Difficulty 5 to 4: Banach-Alaoglu sits exactly where the calibration table puts Tychonoff.

cards.title: Measure what you can, then integrate
cards.hook: Lebesgue's fix was not a better limit theorem. It was cutting the picture the other way.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The set that has no size, and why you have to allow it
cards.hook: You want length to be translation-invariant, countably additive and defined for every set. In 1905 Vitali proved you can have any two.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Solovay's model assumes an inaccessible cardinal; the card now says so.

cards.title: Three theorems that make limits legal
cards.hook: The payoff for giving up on measuring every set: three theorems that let you swap a limit and an integral, with no continuity in sight.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Episode arithmetic: 'four episodes later' is three.

cards.title: Change the ruler and the same sequence stops converging
cards.hook: Convergence is not a property of a sequence. It is a property of a sequence plus the ruler you chose to measure with.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Cross-linked to the completeness card, which shares the C[0,1] example.

cards.title: Press cosine until the calculator stops changing
cards.hook: Type any number into a calculator in radians and press cos over and over. It always lands on 0.7390851332.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Cosine is not a contraction on all of R; fixed that, and the display needs about sixty presses to settle ten digits, not thirty.

cards.title: Shrink every distance and nothing changes
cards.hook: Cap every distance in a space at 1 and nothing topological changes. Boundedness is a fact about your ruler, not about the space.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Remember contractions? That is why value iteration works
cards.hook: Remember that a contraction has exactly one fixed point and iterating finds it? That is the entire convergence proof of value iteration.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: The Bellman operator contracts by at most gamma, not exactly; and the n-step bound carries a 1/(1-gamma) that the body had dropped.

cards.title: Remember the arrows? An epidemic is one trajectory through them
cards.hook: An epidemic does not end because the virus runs out of people. It ends because the susceptible pool crosses a line.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Remember the vector field? Predators and prey live in one
cards.hook: Less fishing during the First World War produced proportionally more sharks. Volterra explained it with a picture of arrows.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: 'the previous card' replaced by naming the phase-portrait idea, since the engine does not guarantee feed order.

cards.title: Ocho años preso, y el mundo tocándole la puerta
cards.hook: Se puede saber si un equilibrio es estable sin resolver la ecuación. Massera demostró el recíproco, y pasó ocho años en una cárcel uruguaya.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Stop solving it and look at the picture
cards.hook: Almost no differential equation has a formula for its solution. Poincaré's answer was to stop asking for one.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Riemann's integral has one fatal habit
cards.hook: Each function in the sequence is integrable. The limit is not. Riemann's integral is not stable under the one operation analysis lives on.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The rationals have a hole you can point at
cards.hook: The rationals have a hole you can point at without ever seeing it. Patching it is the whole content of the real numbers.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: One sequence that converges to every number at once
cards.hook: Can one sequence of real numbers have every point of the unit interval as the limit of one of its subsequences?
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Abel, 1826, and the devil in the translation
cards.hook: Abel's most famous line has a devil in it. The sentence his own editors printed does not.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Rewritten: the 'devil' wording is a sourced translation (Stubhaug), not an unsourceable one, so the card now sets it against the milder sentence printed in Abel's collected works.

cards.title: It diverges, and it takes its time
cards.hook: The harmonic series diverges. Reaching a partial sum of 100 takes about 10^43 terms, which is why nobody has ever watched it happen.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Reorder this sum and get any number you want
cards.hook: The alternating harmonic series sums to ln 2. Reorder the same terms and it sums to 7, or to pi, or to nothing at all.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Cauchy proved it. Abel found the exception.
cards.hook: Cauchy published the proof in 1821. Abel published the exception in 1826. The repair took another twenty years and invented a new idea.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: La escalera que se pega a la diagonal y nunca se le parece
cards.hook: Una escalera de longitud 2 se pega a la diagonal de longitud raíz de 2. ¿En qué momento se pierde la longitud?
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Remember uniform convergence? It is what networks actually promise
cards.hook: The slogan is that a neural network can approximate any function. The theorem behind it is a sentence about uniform convergence.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The first question on Hilbert's list has no answer
cards.hook: Hilbert put it first on his list in 1900. The answer, delivered in two halves, is that the axioms decline to answer.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Difficulty 4→5: the rigor runs countable transitive models, ccc forcing and generic filters — the style guide's own example of level 5.

cards.title: Cut a ball into five pieces, get two balls
cards.hook: Five pieces, no stretching, and you end up with two balls the size of the one you started with.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Two rotations by an irrational angle need not generate a free group; replaced by the standard arccos(1/3) pair. Difficulty 3→4.

cards.title: Counting without counting
cards.hook: A shepherd with no numbers can still tell whether the flock came home. That trick is all of cardinality.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: The grid walk only listed positive rationals; 0 and the negatives now folded in. Dedekind-infinite relabelled a definition, with the choice caveat.

cards.title: Infinity has sizes, and the man who said stop
cards.hook: One of Cantor's Berlin teachers spent twenty years telling the mathematical world that Cantor's infinities were not mathematics.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Kronecker was a Berlin teacher, not Cantor's advisor (Kummer and Weierstrass were); hook fixed. Hilbert quote now given in German with the 1925 lecture / 1926 print dates.

cards.title: La biblioteca de Babel no es infinita, y eso es lo bueno
cards.hook: Borges describe una biblioteca con todos los libros posibles. La cuenta exacta cabe en una línea, y es finita.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Decía que la biblioteca cayó "del lado numerable"; el punto del cuento es que cayó del lado finito.

cards.title: The list nobody can finish
cards.hook: Hand Cantor any list of real numbers and he hands back a number that is not on it. Every time.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: The cases environment had a single backslash where the row break belongs, so the digit rule rendered as one line.

cards.title: There is no last infinity
cards.hook: Every infinity you can name has a bigger one above it, built from it in one move. There is no top.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Turing's proof is Cantor's diagonal in a new costume
cards.hook: The halting problem, Gödel's sentence and Cantor's missing real are one two-line trick in three costumes.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Added the publication note: two instalments in 1936 inside a Proceedings volume dated 1937, so both years are cited in the literature.

cards.title: Gödel found a loophole in the Constitution. Einstein drove.
cards.hook: On the way to his citizenship hearing, Gödel announced he had found a logical flaw in the US Constitution.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: What Gödel actually proved
cards.hook: He let it drop in a closing discussion, almost in passing, and the room moved on. Von Neumann did not.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: The Königsberg remark came in the closing discussion of 7 Sept 1930, not at the end of his own talk. Second theorem now states its content and that it needs more than Q.

cards.title: All horses are the same colour. Find the bug.
cards.hook: The induction is clean, the base case is true, and the conclusion is that all horses are the same colour.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: The sequence that explodes, and dies anyway
cards.hook: A sequence that reaches 10^154 by its third term and still hits zero. Peano arithmetic cannot prove it does.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: A proof that something exists without showing you one
cards.hook: Two irrationals whose power is rational. The proof takes four lines and never tells you which two.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Difficulty 2→3: the rigor leans on Gelfond–Schneider and on excluded middle, not on first-year material.

cards.title: The letter that broke a book already at the printer's
cards.hook: One question, three lines long, arrived while the book answering it was already at the printer's.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Remember the dot product? It was never a product
cards.hook: Row vectors and column vectors have always felt different because they are different kinds of object. An inner product hides the difference.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

reviewed.notes: Reflexivity belongs to the continuous dual of a normed space; said so instead of implying the algebraic dual.

cards.title: The transpose is not about flipping a grid
cards.hook: Why does reversing a product reverse its order under transposition? Because the transpose is an arrow pointing the other way.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Find the smallest pair of matrices these two invariants cannot tell apart
cards.hook: Characteristic polynomial and minimal polynomial are complete invariants for similarity — until they suddenly are not.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Remember diagonalising? Here is what happens when it fails
cards.hook: Not every matrix has enough eigenvectors. The 1s just off the diagonal are not a blemish — they are the missing information.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: A tensor is a machine that turns bilinear into linear
cards.hook: The tensor product exists to do one job: turn every bilinear map into a linear one, in exactly one way.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Multiplying two 2x2 matrices takes seven multiplications, not eight
cards.hook: Matrix multiplication is a tensor, and the fewest multiplications you need is that tensor's rank.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: The determinant is one number because one space is one-dimensional
cards.hook: One sentence explains the permutation sum, the basis-independence and the multiplicativity of the determinant at once.
cards.author: author-math-algebra-1

cards.title: Hardy's proudest boast, aged badly
cards.hook: Hardy's proudest boast was that his subject could never be used for anything. Read it on a banking app.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: The quotation dropped a word. The 1940 text reads "it seems very unlikely"; checked against the printed Apology, not the Wikipedia paraphrase.

cards.title: Public-key cryptography was invented twice, secretly first
cards.hook: A GCHQ mathematician wrote down RSA in 1973. He could not tell anyone for twenty-four years.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Fermat's 1640 letter is three centuries before Cocks, not one.

cards.title: Polynomials can run programs
cards.hook: There is a polynomial whose positive values, as its variables run over the naturals, are exactly the prime numbers.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Added the degree of the Jones–Sato–Wada–Wiens polynomial (25), which the card had left out.

cards.title: Find the smallest positive solution of x² − 61y² = 1
cards.hook: Two unknowns, one equation, small coefficients. Try it by hand and you will not finish this century.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Euclid never argued by contradiction
cards.hook: Everyone reports that Euclid assumed finitely many primes and found a contradiction. He did no such thing.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: "Nothing was contradicted" overstated it: the proof does carry a one-line reductio (q∤1). The point survives — no list of all primes is assumed.

cards.title: Factorisation stops being unique one step outside the integers
cards.hook: In 1847 Lamé announced a proof of Fermat's Last Theorem. It died in the discussion, on one unexamined word.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Unique factorisation in Z[ζ_p] first fails at p=23 (class number 3), not at the first irregular prime 37; Kummer's letter dated 24 May 1847.

cards.title: Which whole numbers are the area of a right triangle?
cards.hook: Is there a right triangle with rational sides and area 1? The honest answer runs through a 1000-year-old question.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: The torsion of E_n is Z/2×Z/2 — the three points with y=0 plus the identity; the card omitted the identity. Difficulty 3→4.

cards.title: La letra del DNI es un teorema disfrazado de trámite
cards.hook: La letra de tu DNI no es un adorno burocrático: es aritmética modular trabajando contra los dedos torpes.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Counted by threes, two left over
cards.hook: Counted by threes, two left over. By fives, three. By sevens, two. A fourth-century puzzle that is now in your phone.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: "Your compiler" does not do multi-modular arithmetic; computer-algebra systems do.

cards.title: Another way for two numbers to be close
cards.hook: In the 2-adic world 1024 is tiny, 1/3 is an ordinary size, and every triangle is isosceles.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: The primes thin out, and they do it on schedule
cards.hook: A number near a million is prime with probability about 1 in 14. Gauss spotted the rule at fifteen, from a table.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: A distractor called √10⁹ "the count of primes you would need to sieve"; it is the largest prime you sieve with.

cards.title: Nine pages from Madras, and the claim in them that was wrong
cards.hook: Hardy received nine pages of unproved formulas from a clerk in Madras. The most confident claim in them was false.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Hardy's quote had a spurious "had". His diagnosis was that Ramanujan assumed ζ has no complex zeros; now attributed to Hardy and sourced to MacTutor.

cards.title: Seventy million, and falling
cards.hook: He was 58, had published nothing in twelve years, and had worked in a Subway. Then he closed the gap.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Zhang's last paper before 2013 was 2001, not 1991 — the body contradicted the card's own hook. The 246 bound is Polymath8b's, on Maynard and Tao's method.

cards.title: Gauss called it golden and proved it eight times
cards.hook: Whether 5 is a square mod 17 secretly depends on whether 17 is a square mod 5. Nothing in the setup suggests it should.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Almost all of them, and almost none we can name
cards.hook: Almost every real number is transcendental. Proving it about any particular number has taken 180 years and counting.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: "Taking n=1 gives e transcendental" is false — with one exponent Lindemann–Weierstrass only says e^α≠0. Replaced with the α=0,1,…,n argument.

cards.title: Riemann turned the primes into a sum over zeros
cards.hook: Riemann wrote eight pages on primes in 1859 and never returned to the subject. We are still working through them.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: The Skewes source was cited but never used; added Skewes's 1933 bound next to the current 1.4×10^316 estimate.

cards.title: The identity where a sum turns into the primes
cards.hook: Euler wrote one equation with a sum on the left and a product over primes on the right. It is the sieve, in ink.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: The lion and his claw
cards.hook: Bernoulli challenged the sharpest mathematicians alive. Newton got the problem at four in the afternoon and had it by four a.m.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Bernoulli did write 'ex ungue Leonem'; it is the 'tanquam' that is David Brewster's 1855 addition (per Whiteside), so the card now names him.

cards.title: The minimum that nobody reaches
cards.hook: Riemann assumed the minimum exists. Weierstrass wrote down a problem where it does not, and the field stalled for thirty years.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The one shape with no ditches
cards.hook: A local minimum tells you nothing about the global one. Convexity is exactly the condition that makes local news global news.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: One inequality wearing several hats
cards.hook: AM-GM, the non-negativity of variance, the Gibbs inequality and half the bounds in information theory are the same inequality wearing hats.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Remember "no ditches"? Deep learning is nothing but ditches
cards.hook: Deep networks violate every hypothesis that makes optimization safe, and gradient descent works anyway. The reasons surprise.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The steepest direction is usually the wrong one
cards.hook: In a narrow valley the gradient points at the wall, not at the exit. That one fact explains momentum, Adam and preconditioning.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The oldest algorithm in machine learning is from 1847
cards.hook: The training loop at the centre of modern machine learning was written down in a two-page note about fitting orbits.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: Every relaxation hands you a certificate
cards.hook: You found a good solution. How would you ever prove nothing better exists, without checking everything else?
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: KKT necessity and sufficiency stated for the differentiable case.

cards.title: Remember the multiplier as a price? Here it is called income
cards.hook: The multiplier in the consumer's problem has a name in every micro course, and nobody mentions that it is the same object.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The multiplier is a price
cards.hook: The multiplier is taught as bookkeeping you throw away at the end. It is usually the number you actually wanted.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: Replaced a distractor that was arguably true (with an equality constraint a zero multiplier does force a zero objective gradient) with a real misconception.

cards.title: Linear programming was invented to cut plywood
cards.hook: A plywood trust in Leningrad asked a young mathematician how to assign work to machines. The answer was linear programming.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: The answer is always at a corner
cards.hook: A linear program has infinitely many feasible points and you only ever have to look at the corners. Then the corners fight back.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

reviewed.notes: An optimum can sit in the middle of a tied face, so corrected to 'a vertex is always among the winners'. Added the degeneracy / anti-cycling caveat to the simplex argument.

cards.title: The homework that was not homework
cards.hook: He arrived late, copied two problems off the board, and handed in the homework a few days later. They were open problems.
cards.author: author-math-analysis-1

cards.title: El cumpleaños compartido de la Selección
cards.hook: Una convocatoria mundialista tiene 23 jugadores. La probabilidad de que dos cumplan el mismo día pasa del 50 %.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: The gambler's complaint that started probability
cards.hook: A French gambler lost money on a bet he had reasoned out carefully, and declared that arithmetic was broken.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: A path that goes everywhere and has a direction nowhere
cards.hook: Bachelier modelled it for stock prices in 1900, five years before Einstein used it to argue that atoms are real. Both beat the mathematics.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Brown watched the particles shaken out of pollen grains, not the grains; and Einstein modelled suspended particles, not pollen.

cards.title: Why the bell curve keeps showing up, and when it doesn't
cards.hook: The bell curve is not a law of nature. It is what a sum looks like when no single term matters much.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Chebyshev is polite. Hoeffding is not.
cards.hook: Chebyshev says you need 250,000 samples. Hoeffding says 27,000. Same question, same data, one extra assumption.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Remember the exponential tail? It is why learning is possible at all
cards.hook: You pay for the number of hypotheses you considered — logarithmically. That logarithm is the whole reason learning works.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: "log|H| extra samples" had the wrong units — the logarithm is paid in the exponent, i.e. log|H|/2ε² samples.

cards.title: Remember multiplying odds? Philosophers made it a definition of rationality
cards.hook: The odds-multiplication you learned as arithmetic is, to philosophers, the definition of not being a fool.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Bayes is a rule for changing your mind
cards.hook: Written in odds, Bayes' theorem stops being a formula to memorise and becomes one multiplication.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: ¿Te acuerdas de multiplicar razones? Eso es el Elo
cards.hook: El puntaje Elo no mide fuerza: mide creencia. Y la actualización después de cada partido es un paso bayesiano.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: One in seventy-three million
cards.hook: A paediatrician squared a probability in court. It cost a woman three years in prison and, eventually, her life.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Remember the prior? An election forecast is one, plus polls
cards.hook: Two forecasters read the same polls and say 1% and 29%. The gap is not the data. It is one assumption.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: Removed an unsourced "standard deviation closer to 4 points" figure; the contrast now rests on what does and does not shrink with n.

cards.title: The expected payout is infinite. What would you pay?
cards.hook: The expected payout is infinite. Name the largest amount you would actually hand over to play once.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Entropy is a question count
cards.hook: Entropy is not disorder. It is the average number of yes/no questions you cannot avoid asking.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Remember the optimal code? Training a model is searching for one
cards.hook: The loss every classifier minimises is the number of extra bits you waste by believing the wrong distribution.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Remember entropy as a question count? It is carved on a gravestone
cards.hook: Shannon's formula and the one on Boltzmann's gravestone differ by a unit conversion. Erasing a bit has a temperature.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: The law of averages is a lie, and the true version is stranger
cards.hook: A million coin flips will leave you about 400 heads ahead or behind. The average converges; the gap grows.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Remember absorbing states? Consensus is one
cards.hook: Nobody in the voter model persuades anybody. Everyone copies at random, and the population still reaches unanimity.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: ¿Te acuerdas de la cadena que olvida dónde empezó? Un pase es un paso
cards.hook: Si una posesión es una cadena de Markov, un pase no vale por bonito: vale por cuánto mueve la probabilidad de gol.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: La matriz canónica tenía una sola barra donde va el salto de fila, así que se renderizaba en una línea.

cards.title: Markov counted 20,000 of Pushkin's letters to win a fight
cards.hook: Markov hand-counted 20,000 letters of Pushkin to win an argument about whether free will exists.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Remember the stationary distribution? Google built a company on it
cards.hook: The two ways a chain fails to forget its start are exactly the two problems PageRank's damping factor fixes.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Where a chain forgets where it started
cards.hook: Run a Markov chain long enough and it forgets where it began. What it remembers is an eigenvector.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

reviewed.notes: The convergence theorem was stated without finiteness, where it needs it (or positive recurrence).

cards.title: You cannot beat a fair game, and the theorem says exactly why
cards.hook: The doubling system really does win almost every time. The theorem explains where the money for that comes from.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Every outcome has probability zero, and one of them happens
cards.hook: Pick a real number uniformly from [0,1]. Every single number had probability zero, and one of them happened.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Death by horse kick, and the shape of rare things
cards.hook: Prussian cavalry deaths by horse kick, 1875–1894. The most famous dataset in statistics is 196 unlucky soldiers.
cards.author: author-math-fnp-1

cards.title: Nobody has ever checked all the open sets
cards.hook: A topology on the plane has more open sets than you can list. You never touch more than a countable handful of them.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Fixed a false claim: the plane has exactly continuum-many open sets, not more than there are reals. Uncountability is the real point.

cards.title: Open depends on where you are standing
cards.hook: The interval from zero to one, half-open, is not open in the line. Shrink the universe to the closed unit interval and it becomes open.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: The obvious way to build a product is the wrong one
cards.hook: Write down the obvious topology on an infinite product and you destroy the only theorem products are for.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: When the inverse map comes for free
cards.hook: Checking that an inverse map is continuous is usually work. On a compact domain with a Hausdorff target it is free.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Why "closed and bounded" was the wrong definition
cards.hook: Infinity is the problem. Compactness is the trick that lets you treat it like something finite.
cards.author: lead

cards.title: Remember the budget set? It is compact, and that is the point
cards.hook: Before anyone proves markets clear, someone has to prove that a consumer has a demand at all. That is a compactness argument.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: The delta that refuses to shrink
cards.hook: A minimum of infinitely many positive numbers can be zero. A minimum of finitely many cannot. That gap is the whole subject.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Two meanings of compact that stopped agreeing
cards.hook: Analysis and topology teach two different definitions of compact and never mention it, because in metric spaces they agree.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Remember compactness? It is why Nash equilibria exist
cards.hook: The footnote that said existence follows from Kakutani's theorem is the compactness card you already read.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: A space in one piece you cannot walk across
cards.hook: One piece, two points, and no path between them. The gap is infinitely thin and infinitely long.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Fixed a number: between x=0.001 and 0.002 sin(1/x) completes about eighty oscillations, not hundreds of swings.

cards.title: The intermediate value theorem is not about numbers
cards.hook: You proved the intermediate value theorem with a least upper bound. The supremum was never doing the work.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Tightened the non-interval separation: the two outer points have to be in the subspace.

cards.title: Two places on the equator, same temperature
cards.hook: Right now there are two points exactly opposite each other on the equator with exactly the same temperature. Why must that be true?
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: What survives when you delete the middle forever
cards.hook: Delete middle thirds forever and you remove the whole length of the interval. What is left has as many points as you started with.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Added the nonempty clause to Brouwer characterisation of the Cantor set.

cards.title: Why continuity had to be defined backwards
cards.hook: Continuity is stated with preimages, not images. That is not a convention — images cannot carry a topology.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: How to prove two shapes are different
cards.hook: Proving two spaces are the same means building a map. Proving they differ means finding one thing that cannot survive the trip.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Je le vois, mais je ne le crois pas
cards.hook: Cantor found a bijection between a line and a square, and broke into French mid-letter to tell Dedekind about it.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Hook no longer claims to know why Cantor switched to French; nobody does.

cards.title: The coffee cup is a bad first lesson
cards.hook: The mug turning into a donut is true, and it teaches three wrong things about what homeomorphism means.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Covering spaces are Galois theory in disguise
cards.hook: Subgroups of the fundamental group correspond to covering spaces, order-reversing. You have seen this lattice before, in algebra.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Unroll the circle into a line
cards.hook: To prove a loop cannot be undone, stop looking at the circle and look at the line spiralling above it.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Remember fixed points? A crowd agreeing is one
cards.hook: Remember fixed points? A room full of people talking until they agree is converging to one, and you can name whose opinion wins.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Softened 'exactly eigenvector centrality' to the recursion s_i = sum_j s_j T_ji (Wikipedia states the recursion, not the term); fixed-point wording; varied the opener.

cards.title: Crumple the map and one point is still honest
cards.hook: Crumple a map of Bogotá and drop it on the floor of Bogotá. One point of the paper lies exactly over the place it names.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: El topólogo sin manos que fundó una escuela
cards.hook: Perdió las dos manos en un accidente industrial en 1907, se pasó a las matemáticas y terminó fundando la topología mexicana.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Remember the crumpled map? It is why prices can clear
cards.hook: Remember the fixed point in the crumpled map? Arrow and Debreu used the same theorem to prove that market-clearing prices exist.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Cut the space in two, glue the groups
cards.hook: With two trees instead of one, going around A then B is genuinely different from B then A — and the difference is a loop around nothing.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Added the missing van Kampen hypothesis (U and V path connected) and the two-arc cover of the circle that shows why it is needed.

cards.title: Hang a picture so that either nail drops it
cards.hook: Wind the string so the picture hangs on two nails, and pulling out either nail — either one — drops it.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Continuous maps turn into homomorphisms
cards.hook: Turn a continuous map into a group homomorphism and an impossible group identity becomes an impossible map.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: The dog, the tree and the leash
cards.hook: The leash is wrapped around the tree. Nothing about its shape says so — the only surviving information is: once around, this way.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Turn it twice and the tangle disappears
cards.hook: Rotate the cup on your palm once and your arm is twisted. Rotate it again the same way and everything is back to normal.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: It took until 1911 to prove a line is not a plane
cards.hook: Cantor found a bijection from a line to a square, Peano a continuous surjection. Proving dimension is real took until 1911.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: The fundamental group is blind to a beach ball
cards.hook: Every loop on a sphere shrinks to a point, exactly as on a solid ball. The sphere still has a hole; loops are the wrong probe.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Three colours are enough to prove a knot
cards.hook: You cannot prove a knot is knotted by trying to untie it. You can prove it with three crayons.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Credited Alexander and Briggs (1926) alongside Reidemeister, and tightened the knot-group statement to surjections sending meridians to transpositions.

cards.title: Remember knots? Your cells employ a professional untangler
cards.hook: Remember that knottedness lives in the complement, not the curve? Your cells run an enzyme whose whole job is knot theory.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Four dimensions has uncountably many calculuses
cards.hook: Every Euclidean space has exactly one way to do calculus on it. Except four-dimensional space, which has uncountably many.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Corrected an overreach: exotic smooth structures also exist on spheres (Milnor 1956). R^4 is unique among Euclidean spaces, not among all manifolds.

cards.title: Perelmán resolvió el problema y dijo que no
cards.hook: Subió la solución a arXiv sin enviarla a ninguna revista, y después dijo que no al millón de dólares y a la Medalla Fields.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: The two clauses in the definition nobody explains
cards.hook: A manifold looks locally like Euclidean space. Then the definition adds two clauses that look like paperwork and are not.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Two fixes: proper initial segments of the long ray are homeomorphic to [0,1), not R; and paracompactness excludes the long line rather than keeping it.

cards.title: Does your space secretly have a ruler?
cards.hook: Two conditions that never mention distance decide whether a distance exists. The proof does not guess a metric — it borrows one.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Spelled out that regular is Munkres regular (T1 included), since the statement is false under the weaker convention.

cards.title: The exact price of a distance function
cards.hook: Three mathematicians on three continents settled the exact condition for a topology to come from a distance, inside two years.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Hook said eighteen months; Nagata 1950, Smirnov 1951 and Bing 1951 are only pinned to the year, so it now says inside two years.

cards.title: Change one bracket and the real line breaks
cards.hook: Flip one bracket in the definition of an interval and the real line stops admitting any distance function at all.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Distance was never the point
cards.hook: Every epsilon-delta proof you ever wrote used the distance for exactly one thing. Topology keeps that thing and throws the ruler away.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: There are 355 topologies on four points
cards.hook: There are exactly 355 topologies on a four-element set, 6,942 on five, and no known formula for the next one.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: The man who named topology lost the strip
cards.hook: The man who invented the word topology also found the Möbius strip in 1858. The strip is not named after him.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: The line with two zeros
cards.hook: Glue two copies of the real line along everything but zero. Every point still looks like an interval, and the two zeros are inseparable.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Una botella que solo cabe en cuatro dimensiones
cards.hook: No es una botella, y el nombre probablemente venga de una palabra mal traducida. Lo que sí es seguro es que no cabe en tres dimensiones.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: La etimologia Flaeche/Flasche no esta documentada (la Wikipedia inglesa ya no la recoge); ahora va marcada como leyenda.
