cards.title: A continuous function built out of nothing but open sets
cards.hook: No distance, no formula, nothing to compute with — and out comes a continuous function. Urysohn was 26 when he drowned.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: A sequence that converges to every point at once
cards.hook: The sequence 1, 2, 3, 4, ... can converge to every real number at once. Uniqueness of limits is an axiom, not a fact.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: The property that breaks when you square it
cards.hook: Hausdorff, regular, compact and connected all survive products. Normality fails, and it fails on a space times itself.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Reworded open boxes as open sets, to avoid colliding with the box topology.

cards.title: Infinitely many compact spaces, multiplied
cards.hook: A product of compact spaces is compact — even an uncountable one. The theorem is not merely proved with choice; it is equivalent to it.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

reviewed.notes: Added the Kelley 1950 source (DOI verified via Crossref) and his actual construction for Tychonoff implies AC.

cards.title: Why logicians stole the word compactness
cards.hook: Model theory has a compactness theorem. The name is not a metaphor — it is the same theorem, about an actual compact space.
cards.author: author-math-topology-1

cards.title: Remember the point at infinity? Florence got there first.
cards.hook: Painters were drawing the point at infinity for two hundred years before a mathematician admitted it was a point.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Your coffee is a plant's chemical weapon, badly aimed
cards.hook: The coffee plant did not make caffeine for you. It made it to poison insects and sterilise the soil around itself.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Softened the afternoon-crash mechanism from stated fact to the usual explanation.

cards.title: El campesino más famoso del mundo nunca existió
cards.hook: Juan Valdez lo inventó una agencia de Nueva York en 1958. Fue la mejor política económica del café colombiano.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: A game you can teach in five minutes and lose at for fifty years
cards.hook: Go's rules fit on a postcard. The number of legal positions has 171 digits.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Go did not fall to brute force: AlphaGo won in 2016 with a neural network, not search. Corrected and trimmed to length.

cards.title: The board game designed as propaganda against itself
cards.hook: Monopoly was invented to teach you that landlords are the problem. It came with a second rule set nobody plays.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Parker Brothers' token run of The Landlord's Game was 1939; sequencing corrected.

cards.title: The salt in your salary is a rumour
cards.hook: Salary really does come from the Latin for salt. Roman soldiers really were not paid in salt.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: One man in Baghdad named two-thirds of your maths vocabulary
cards.hook: Algebra is named after a book about setting broken bones. Algorithm is named after the man who wrote it.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Softened an unverifiable superlative about the word 'algorithm'.

cards.title: The one word almost every language agrees on
cards.hook: Ten unrelated languages, five continents, one nearly identical syllable for "I did not catch that".
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: En 2010 el español perdió dos letras
cards.hook: La RAE prometió en 1713 limpiar y fijar el idioma. Trescientos años después su mejor trabajo ha sido ceder.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: 'Siglo y medio' was wrong: ch and ll were letters from the 1754 Ortografia until 2010.

cards.title: La letra que inventó la pereza y que Bruselas casi borra
cards.hook: La ñ nació como una trampa de copistas con prisa. En 1991 Bruselas estuvo a punto de borrarla por libre comercio.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Title reworded for grammar; the 1991 EEC keyboard dispute and the decree of 23 April 1993 check out.

cards.title: Un país, tres segundas personas
cards.hook: En Medellín te dicen vos, en Bogotá usted y en Cartagena tú. Los tres son restos de la misma pelea del siglo XVI.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Fixed a tu/vos mix inside one clause ('uses ... venis').

cards.title: There is no English word for the best part of lunch
cards.hook: English can describe sitting at the table long after the plates are cleared. It just needs a whole sentence to do it.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Hook's 'eleven words' did not count out; replaced.

cards.title: The alphabet that draws the inside of your mouth
cards.hook: Korean consonants are not arbitrary squiggles. Each one is a small drawing of what your tongue is doing.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: A man who could not read invented a writing system
cards.hook: Sequoyah could not read a word of any language. He worked out what writing was from first principles, and then built one.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The circle of fifths is not a circle
cards.hook: Go up twelve perfect fifths and you should land seven octaves higher. You land a quarter of a semitone past it.

series.title: Why the piano is a lie

cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The piano in tune is the piano lying evenly
cards.hook: A perfectly tuned piano has no pure thirds, and its octaves are deliberately too wide.

series.title: Why the piano is a lie

cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Somewhere on your keyboard, a wolf is living
cards.hook: You cannot destroy the comma. You can only decide which chord has to carry it — and that decision picks which keys exist.

series.title: Why the piano is a lie

cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: El metro que Bogotá construyó con buses
cards.hook: Bogotá resolvió su metro sin construir un metro: buses, pero con derechos de vía de tren.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: In Bogotá, boiling water is not hot enough
cards.hook: At 2,625 metres, a rolling boil is about nine degrees cooler than the one your recipe assumes.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The only habitable place on Earth that nobody claims
cards.hook: Two countries, two border lines, and one patch of desert that each of them insists belongs to the other.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: A border that goes through a front door, and then a shed
cards.hook: One town, twenty-two Belgian exclaves, and seven Dutch enclaves inside those. The border runs through a front door.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: How many Greenlands fit inside Africa?
cards.hook: On the wall map they look the same size. Commit to a number before you read on.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Greenland is not the size of Africa, and Mercator knew
cards.hook: Mercator's map is not a bad picture of the world. It is a very good picture of a compass bearing.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Added the reciprocal related link to the Greenland challenge card.

cards.title: Remember counting the complement? It explains why coincidences are boring.
cards.hook: Twenty-three people in a room, and the odds of a shared birthday are better than even. Count pairs, not people.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Absorbed the 253-people / 253-pairs coincidence from a rejected near-duplicate fact card.

cards.title: He arrived at your door and said your brain was open
cards.hook: No house, no job, no possessions beyond a suitcase — and roughly 1,500 papers with more than 500 co-authors.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: He rebuilt geometry, then spent forty years walking away from it
cards.hook: In 2010 the greatest geometer of the century wrote to demand that his own work be removed from every library.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The Poincaré conjecture was solved on a preprint server
cards.hook: He solved a hundred-year-old problem, posted it for free, and turned down a million dollars and the Fields Medal.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Virginia Woolf, in a false beard, inspecting the Royal Navy
cards.hook: Six people in fancy dress talked their way onto Britain's most secret warship, speaking a language they invented on the train.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: "Intellectually lazy"
cards.hook: A physicist wrote nonsense about quantum gravity, got it published, and then explained why he had done it.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The forgery of a forgery outsold the original
cards.hook: A fake stone giant earned its maker a fortune. Then a fake of the fake earned more, and both drew queues.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Hull's argument was at a Methodist revival meeting, not with his cousin; inflation figure corrected.

cards.title: Nobody burned the Library of Alexandria
cards.hook: The great fire that destroyed the Library of Alexandria is the tidiest story in ancient history, and probably did not happen.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Fifteen hundred years ahead of schedule, then dropped in the sea
cards.hook: A lump of corroded bronze from a Roman-era shipwreck turned out to contain thirty gears and an eclipse calendar.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The bet you are guaranteed to lose
cards.hook: If your degrees of belief break the probability axioms, a stranger can sell you bets you each call fair and still take your money.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Opened on a definition; reordered so the Dutch book exploit leads and the credence framing follows.

cards.title: The test came back positive. Now what?
cards.hook: A test that is right 90% of the time just came back positive. Your turn: how worried should you be?
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Recall asked for a count and the reveal answered with a share; question aligned.

cards.title: Three pages in 1963, and the definition collapsed
cards.hook: Three pages, two examples, and a definition that had stood since Plato stopped working.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Every emerald you have ever seen is also grue
cards.hook: Every emerald ever examined is green. Every emerald ever examined is also grue. Pick one, and you have predicted different futures.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: The rigor quantified over an undefined predicate Ex'; renotated with Mx for 'is an emerald'.

cards.title: The sun has made you no promises
cards.hook: Ask why the sun will rise tomorrow and every answer you give quietly assumes the thing it is supposed to prove.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Nobody in 1967 was asking about a lever
cards.hook: In Foot's original case you are the driver, not a bystander, and the paper is not about trolleys at all.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: If you are so clever, why aren't you rich?
cards.hook: The first philosopher answered the question 'if you are so clever, why aren't you rich?' by cornering a market.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: The sentence that cannot be either
cards.hook: Nine words that no consistent theory of truth can survive: this sentence is not true.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Difficulty 2 to 3: the rigor is the diagonal lemma plus Tarski undefinability with Godel numbering.

cards.title: The man who memorised the whole rulebook
cards.hook: Searle's reply to his critics was to swallow the room: memorise every rule, work outdoors, still understand nothing.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Remember Gödel's sentence? It does not prove you are not a machine
cards.hook: Remember Gödel's unprovable sentence? Two well-known arguments use it to prove you are not a machine, and both leak in the same place.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Difficulty 2 to 3: the rigor turns on Con(F) and the second incompleteness theorem.

cards.title: Ariel, Calibán y quién decide el símbolo
cards.hook: Rodó le dio a América Latina un símbolo en 1900. Setenta años después, Fernández Retamar le devolvió el que el maestro había descartado.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: 1898 corrected: the US did not keep Cuba. Puerto Rico and the Philippines were ceded; Cuba was under military occupation. Trimmed back inside the word limit.

cards.title: El problema del indio no era el indio
cards.hook: Mariátegui movió la pregunta indígena de la moral y la escuela a un solo lugar: la propiedad de la tierra.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Two questions that sound like one
cards.hook: Free from what, and free to do what, are not two halves of one question. Berlin thought the second one had a body count.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Liberty upsets patterns
cards.hook: Start from whatever distribution you think is perfectly just. Nozick shows it survives about one basketball season.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Choose the rules before you know who you will be
cards.hook: Design the society first, then find out who you are in it. Rawls turns fairness into a decision problem under uncertainty.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Justice is the first virtue of social institutions
cards.hook: The opening line of the most important work of political philosophy of the twentieth century.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Remember falsifiability? Here is a field that stopped doing it
cards.hook: Remember falsifiability? The replication crisis is what a field looks like when it keeps Popper's words and drops his procedure.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: What would have to happen for you to give this up?
cards.hook: Popper's question is one line long and it still sorts the room: what observation would make you abandon this?
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: The word that got away from the man who coined it
cards.hook: Kuhn wrote a book about how key terms shift meaning across revolutions. A critic counted twenty-one meanings of his own key term inside it.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: All models are wrong, but some are useful
cards.hook: The most quoted sentence in statistics. The clause that does the work is the second one.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Hook claimed people usually drop the second clause, which is not true - the line is quoted whole. Rewritten to point at which clause does the work.

cards.title: They blamed the pigeons
cards.hook: They cleaned the antenna, evicted the pigeons, and the hiss was still there. It was the oldest light in the universe.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The stars at the edge are moving much too fast
cards.hook: The outer stars of a galaxy orbit as fast as the inner ones. By every rule we know, they should be flung off.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The Higgs gives you about one percent of your mass
cards.hook: The Higgs field is described as the thing that gives matter mass. It is responsible for about one percent of yours.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Dear radioactive ladies and gentlemen
cards.hook: Pauli invented a particle to save conservation of energy, admitted it might be undetectable, and skipped the meeting for a ball.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Iron is where the energy runs out
cards.hook: Fusion and fission release energy for the same reason, and they run in opposite directions. The turning point is iron.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Everything you have ever touched is three particles
cards.hook: Every object you have ever held is built from three particles. The Standard Model contains seventeen, and nobody knows why.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Reconciled the headline seventeen particles with the twelve gauge bosons in the rigor: species versus states.

cards.title: ¿Cuánta potencia produce un metro cúbico del centro del Sol?
cards.hook: El centro del Sol produce menos calor por metro cúbico que una pila de compost. Y sin embargo ahí está.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: 276.5 W/m3 is the peak at the centre. Dropped the unverified reptile comparison; added that the core is 1.5% of the volume and the whole-Sun average is 0.27 W/m3.

cards.title: What if you had one percent more electrons than your friend?
cards.hook: Matter is electrically neutral to absurd precision. Break that by one percent and the numbers stop being human.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Los electrones van a paso de caracol y la luz se prende ya
cards.hook: Los electrones en el cable de tu lámpara avanzan más lento que un caracol. La luz se prende de todos modos al instante.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Why the sky is blue — and why that's only two thirds of the answer
cards.hook: Violet scatters more than blue. So why isn't the sky violet? The honest answer needs two extra facts, and both are about you.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Body claimed blue scatters nine times more than red; nine is the violet-to-red ratio. Reworded to agree with the rigor.

cards.title: The twitch that became the entire electrical grid
cards.hook: Faraday's needle only moved when he connected the battery and when he disconnected it. Steady current did nothing at all.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The speed of light fell out of an equation about magnets
cards.hook: Maxwell patched an inconsistency in four equations. A wave equation fell out, and its speed matched the measured speed of light.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Cross-linked with the Maxwell quote card through related, so the shared door is explicit rather than a hidden near-duplicate.

cards.title: The year the patent clerk had four ideas
cards.hook: In one year a 26-year-old patent examiner published four papers. Three founded new fields. He got the job because academia had rejected him.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Brownian motion: Einstein's paper is about suspended grains in general, so Brown's 1827 observation is now credited explicitly rather than implied.

cards.title: The sentence where optics stopped being its own subject
cards.hook: Maxwell worked out how fast waves would travel in his model of magnetism. He recognised the number from a different science.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Cross-linked with the Maxwell idea card through related.

cards.title: The eight minutes that cost astronomy its circles
cards.hook: Kepler's circular orbit for Mars was wrong by eight minutes of arc. He refused to round it away.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Fermi's scraps of paper
cards.hook: While the shock wave arrived, Fermi dropped torn paper and watched how far it blew. He had the yield before the instruments did.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The island with no pollen
cards.hook: Heisenberg went to a treeless island to escape his hay fever. He came back with a theory whose multiplication does not commute.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: La tesis que decía que el Sol es hidrógeno
cards.hook: En 1925 una estudiante descubrió de qué está hecho el Sol. Su director la convenció de escribir que el resultado casi seguro no era real.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The blocks that are never all there
cards.hook: Energy is not a substance. It is a number you can only find by inventing the right places to look for it.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: El avión no vuela por lo que te enseñaron en el colegio
cards.hook: La explicación del ala que te enseñaron en el colegio es falsa, y la NASA tiene una página entera dedicada a decirlo.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Difficulty 1 to 2: the rigor is circulation and Kutta-Joukowski, past the no-equations bar for level 1. NASA Incorrect Lift Theory page verified live and supporting.

cards.title: How much gravity is there where astronauts float?
cards.hook: Astronauts float 400 km up. Guess how much of Earth's gravity reaches them: 0%, 10% or 90%?
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The lifeguard who does calculus of variations on the way to the water
cards.hook: Throw away forces. Assign one number to each possible history of the world, and physics becomes a problem about finding a stationary point.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The New York Times owed a rocket an apology for 49 years
cards.hook: In 1920 the New York Times explained that rockets cannot work in space. It ran the correction 49 years later.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: You are doing 1,670 km/h right now and your coffee doesn't care
cards.hook: Bogotá is moving at about 1,670 km/h and you cannot feel a thing. That is not a failure of your senses.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Why every gentle wobble in the universe is the same wobble
cards.hook: A pendulum, a guitar string, a bond between two atoms and a radio circuit obey one equation. That is not a coincidence.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The cat that turns over without ever starting to spin
cards.hook: Drop a cat upside down with no spin at all. Conservation of angular momentum says it can never start spinning. It lands on its feet anyway.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Dropped the unverifiable sixty frames a second; kept 1894 and the Academy's Comptes Rendus, added the documented objection that the cat pushed off the handler's hand.

cards.title: Every symmetry pays you a conserved quantity
cards.hook: The books balance because the laws of physics do not care what day it is. That indifference is worth exactly one conserved number.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Klein read it out because she was not a member of the society (was: not allowed to speak); paper source now points to the Tavel translation rather than a wiki page.

cards.title: Remember groups? Physics pays you for every one of them
cards.hook: You learned that a group is a set of symmetries. Here is the invoice: each continuous one hands physics a quantity that cannot change.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The prize Poincaré paid to destroy
cards.hook: Poincaré won the King of Sweden's prize in 1889. Then he found the error, and paid more than the prize to burn the print run.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Prize date softened to January 1889: the cited Mittag-Leffler page dates the announcement 20 January. The 2500 kr prize, 3500 kr bill, two copies and the inscription all verified.

cards.title: The game you cannot win more than 75% of the time
cards.hook: A two-player game with a hard ceiling of 75%. Share entangled particles and you win 85.4% of the time, every time.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The honest scoreboard on what any of it means
cards.hook: What quantum mechanics means is genuinely unsettled. What it predicts is not. Keeping those apart is the whole trick.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Identical predictions now attributed to those three interpretations only, and objective collapse added in the rigor as the one family that is testable rather than argued.

cards.title: The number carved on Schwinger's tombstone
cards.hook: Two physicists in this packet have equations on their gravestones. Schwinger's is the first correction to the electron's magnetism.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: 0.13 parts per trillion is the precision on g/2, not on the anomaly; restated as g/2 = 1.00115965218059(13) per Fan et al 2023.

cards.title: Planck called it an act of despair
cards.hook: Planck did not believe in quanta. He introduced them to make a formula work and spent years trying to get rid of them.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: A quantum computer is not a parallel computer
cards.hook: "It tries every answer at once" is the wrong picture. If that were all it did, you would read out a random answer.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Hydrogen's colours are eigenvalues you can photograph
cards.hook: Why is the light from hydrogen a set of sharp lines instead of a smear? Because you are looking at a spectrum in the linear-algebra sense.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Why you don't sink through the floor
cards.hook: Solidity is not electrical repulsion. It is a bookkeeping rule about which states exist, and it holds up white dwarfs too.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Chandrasekhar's 1930 shipboard work began the calculation; the 1.4 solar-mass value needs the corrected mean molecular weight. Reworded.

cards.title: A state is a vector. A measurement is a choice of basis.
cards.hook: Superposition sounds mystical until you notice it means "not parallel to the basis you happened to pick".
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: You met the uncertainty principle in your analysis course
cards.hook: A click contains every frequency; a pure tone lasts forever. You met the uncertainty principle in analysis, before anyone mentioned physics.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: One electron at a time, and the stripes show up anyway
cards.hook: Send electrons through two slits one at a time. Each lands as a single dot. The dots assemble into stripes anyway.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Merli and Tonomura used an electron biprism, not literal slits; added Bach et al 2013 with source. Electron wavelength is a twentieth of an atomic diameter, not a hundredth.

cards.title: The black hole was solved in a trench
cards.hook: Weeks after Einstein published general relativity, a 42-year-old artillery lieutenant on the Russian front sent him the exact solution.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The most famous equation in physics was an afterthought
cards.hook: The most famous equation in physics was a three-page footnote Einstein sent in three months after the paper everyone remembers.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: June 1905 was the submission of the relativity paper, not its appearance; reworded.

cards.title: Un gramo de cualquier cosa son 21 kilotones
cards.hook: La bomba de Hiroshima convirtió en energía menos de un gramo de masa. El resto del artefacto sobró.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Remember curvature? That's all gravity ever was
cards.hook: You learned to detect curvature without leaving the surface. Einstein's move was to say gravity is exactly that, and nothing else.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The wiggle that was a four-hundredth of a proton wide
cards.hook: Two black holes collided 1.3 billion years ago. The news arrived as a four-kilometre ruler changing length by a four-hundredth of a proton.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: 4e-18 m is the difference between the two arms (hL), not one arm's change (hL/2); made explicit in body and rigor. Added the February 2016 announcement.

cards.title: The distance between two different events can be zero
cards.hook: Two different events can be at zero distance from each other. That single minus sign is what makes causality geometric.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The most successful failed experiment ever run
cards.hook: They floated a five-foot slab of sandstone on mercury to measure Earth's motion through the aether. They measured nothing, twice.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The equations don't know which way time runs. Your coffee does.
cards.hook: Film a pendulum and run it backwards: fine. Film an egg and run it backwards: absurd. The underlying equations cannot tell the difference.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The Boltzmann factor is the shape of the sky
cards.hook: The atmosphere thins with height by exactly the factor that governs chemical reaction rates. Same exponential, same reason.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Remember Shannon entropy? Physics wrote it first, in joules
cards.hook: Shannon's entropy is measured in bits. Gibbs's entropy is measured in joules per kelvin. The formula is identical.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Gibbs entropy dated to his 1902 statistical mechanics, not the 1870s work on heterogeneous substances.

cards.title: The equation carved above Boltzmann's head
cards.hook: There is an equation carved on a grave in Vienna. Boltzmann never wrote it in that form — Planck did.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The one invention a patent office won't read about
cards.hook: There is exactly one kind of invention the US patent office refuses to consider without a working model in the room.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The demon was beaten by its own notebook
cards.hook: Maxwell's demon sorts molecules and breaks the second law. It took 115 years to find the flaw, and the flaw was its memory.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: Nobody told the atoms to do it all at once
cards.hook: Each atom obeys a smooth rule and talks only to its neighbours. Somehow the whole sheet of them changes state at one exact temperature.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: The air in your room is allowed to suffocate you
cards.hook: Nothing in Newton's laws forbids all the air in your room moving into one corner. It is allowed. Here is how often it happens.
cards.author: author-physics-1

reviewed.notes: Two arithmetic errors fixed: the exponent has 27 digits not 26, and the relative fluctuation at N=2.5e25 is 2e-13 not 6e-13. Recall reworded to match.

cards.title: The block that was hiding inside anything warm
cards.hook: Rumford bored cannon barrels for a living and noticed the brass stayed hot as long as the horses kept walking.
cards.author: author-physics-1

cards.title: El No ganó por 53.894 votos
cards.hook: El 2 de octubre de 2016 el No le ganó al Sí por 53.894 votos, con 37% de participación.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: The vote totals did not differ by the 53.894 the title claims. Replaced with the Registraduria escrutinio: No 6.431.376 (50,21%), Si 6.377.482 (49,78%), margin 53.894.

cards.title: La paz que consistió en repartirse el poder
cards.hook: Liberales y conservadores acordaron turnarse la presidencia durante dieciséis años. Funcionó, y ese fue el problema.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: The 1957 plebiscite approved paridad, not alternacion; alternacion came from the 1958-59 constitutional reform. Diagram accents fixed.

cards.title: Arrow proved the repair shop is empty
cards.hook: Condorcet found one broken rule. Arrow proved that the repair shop is empty.

series.title: Why democracy is hard to define

cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Episode had no curiosity gap into episode 4; added one on giving up a condition.

cards.title: Remember social choice? There is a second impossibility
cards.hook: Arrow killed the perfect voting rule. Gibbard and Satterthwaite killed the honest one.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: The majority can want A over B, B over C, and C over A
cards.hook: Three voters, three options, and the majority prefers A to B, B to C, and C to A.

series.title: Why democracy is hard to define

cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Episode pointed forward to episode 4 and skipped episode 3; gap rewritten to hand off to the repair attempt.

cards.title: An impossibility theorem is a list of things you can give up
cards.hook: Arrow's theorem has four hypotheses. Democracies survive by breaking one of them on purpose.

series.title: Why democracy is hard to define

cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Same ballots, three rules, three winners
cards.hook: Twenty-one voters, three candidates, one set of ballots. Three different rules, three different winners.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: The rule that manufactures two parties
cards.hook: The clearest near-law in political science: count votes this way and you get two parties, whatever the voters wanted.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Why both candidates walk to the middle
cards.hook: Two ice-cream carts on a beach end up side by side in the middle. So do two parties.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Diagram text referred to 'voter 3' but the median dot was labelled only 'median voter'; relabelled.

cards.title: Almost every government on earth calls itself a democracy
cards.hook: The German Democratic Republic built a wall to keep its citizens in, and kept the word in its name.

series.title: Why democracy is hard to define

cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Recall duplicated the Athens fact card, and one distractor ('Athens spent heavily on jury pay') is true. Replaced with an item on Gallie's contested concept; cards cross-linked.

cards.title: La papeleta que nadie autorizó
cards.hook: En 1990 unos estudiantes metieron en las urnas una papeleta que ninguna ley contemplaba. Dos años después el país tenía otra constitución.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: Una hoja de papel contra el Estado
cards.hook: Sin abogado, en una hoja escrita a mano, y el juez tiene diez días para responder. Así funciona la tutela.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: 1.150 'familias' changed to 'nucleos familiares', the Corte's own count in T-025/2004.

cards.title: Two branches, both elected, no referee
cards.hook: Linz's argument against presidentialism in one line: two elected branches, both claiming the people, and no referee.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Opened on the publication rather than the claim; first sentence rewritten to lead with the dual-mandate problem.

cards.title: Why the group with more members usually loses
cards.hook: Sugar producers are few and organised; sugar consumers are millions and silent. Olson explained why that is the normal case.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Olson's typology is three-way (privileged/intermediate/latent). Ostrom principles 4 and 7 restated correctly, and inshore fisheries are her failure cases - replaced with the Philippine zanjeras.

cards.title: Two towns, one fence, three times the income
cards.hook: Same desert, same families, same food, and one side of the fence earns several times the other.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

reviewed.notes: Easterly reviewed the book warmly; his objection is ex-post rationalising and reliance on anecdote, not cherry-picked cases. Corrected.

cards.title: The power you can measure is the weakest kind
cards.hook: The strongest kind of power leaves no trace: nobody fought, because nobody thought of fighting.
cards.author: author-humanities-1

cards.title: The accountant who proved passing was pointless, wrongly
cards.hook: The first man to put football in a spreadsheet used it to argue against passing. His data said the opposite.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Nobody has ever scored 0.79 of a goal
cards.hook: Every penalty in Opta's model is worth exactly 0.79 goals. Not this penalty — penalties.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Remember graphs? A football team is one, and it has a cut vertex.
cards.hook: Eleven vertices, a few hundred directed edges. A football team is a small weighted digraph that runs for ninety minutes.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Brandes is O(|V||E|) only unweighted; added the weighted bound, since the card uses weights.

cards.title: The best pass on the pitch is often the one nobody made
cards.hook: Draw the map of everywhere your team would win the ball if it landed there. Football turns into a weather chart.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Two Poissons get football almost exactly right, and fail at 0–0
cards.hook: Model goals as two independent Poisson counts and you predict almost every scoreline correctly — except the ones that decide seasons.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Corrected which scorelines independent Poissons misfit (0-0 and 1-1 are under-predicted, not 1-0/0-1); added the negative sign of rho; repaired broken KaTeX cases rows.

cards.title: The pass that made the goal possible gets nothing
cards.hook: Expected goals prices the 25 shots in a match and nothing else. So what is the pass that made the goal possible worth?
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Hook's unsourced '1,500 actions a match' cut; kept Opta's verified 25 shots.

cards.title: Remember absorbing Markov chains? A football possession is one.
cards.hook: An absorbing chain asks: starting here, where do I end up? Football asks: starting here, do I score?
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Repaired a broken KaTeX block matrix (missing row break).

cards.title: A number that goes down when you press harder
cards.hook: PPDA measures a press with a ratio anyone can compute. That is exactly why it gets misread.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: PPDA dated to Colin Trainor's StatsBomb article of July 2014, not 'around 2013'.

cards.title: The ranking you could climb by not playing
cards.hook: Romania hired a ranking consultant and then refused to play football. It worked.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Remember Bayes? Every Elo rating is a posterior that forgot its error bars.
cards.hook: New rating = old rating + K × (what happened − what you expected). That is Bayes with the variance nailed shut.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Elo's own model used a normal curve; the logistic form came later. Corrected.

cards.title: El 5-0, y después
cards.hook: En 1993 Colombia le ganó 5-0 a Argentina en Buenos Aires y Pelé la puso como favorita del Mundial. Nueve meses después todo se había ido.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Vague 'amenazas' replaced by the documented Gabriel Jaime Gomez threats; sentence reduction specified (43 to 23 anos); added Argentina's 33-match home record.

cards.title: Cinco años en los que Bogotá fue la capital del fútbol mundial
cards.hook: Entre 1949 y 1954 el mejor fútbol del mundo se jugó en Bogotá, y fue porque Colombia estaba expulsada de la FIFA.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: El 16 de julio de 1950 no hubo final
cards.hook: Brasil solo necesitaba empatar. Uruguay ganó 2-1 y ciento setenta mil personas salieron del estadio en silencio.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Varela's line found verbatim in the source, so it is now a real quotation.

cards.title: Cuatro minutos, dos goles, un problema moral
cards.hook: Cuatro minutos separan el gol más tramposo del Mundial del mejor gol de la historia. Los hizo el mismo hombre.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Three became two, and the centre-back was born
cards.hook: One word changed in the offside law in 1925. English football scored 1,673 more goals the next season.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Cut the unsourced 'offside forty times a match'; WM dominance corrected to standard from the late 1930s and lasting a generation.

cards.title: The World Cup was found by a dog called Pickles
cards.hook: Scotland Yard could not find the World Cup. A dog sniffing a hedge in South London found it in seven days.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Dropped the unsourceable comparison with England's winning bonus; replaced with Corbett's and Pickles's documented rewards.

cards.title: Remember efficient markets? Football odds are the cleanest test ever built.
cards.hook: A bookmaker's odds are a probability forecast with money behind it — and they add up to more than one on purpose.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The referees changed, and nobody had told them anything
cards.hook: A tragedy in Catania emptied Italian stadiums in 2007 — and handed economists the cleanest test of crowd pressure ever run.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The best experiment in sports science was an accident
cards.hook: In 2020 football played 83 Bundesliga matches with nobody watching. Home advantage went negative.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: Four flips, and the coin appears to hate streaks
cards.hook: A fair coin, four flips, one innocent-looking question. The answer is not one half, and it took 33 years to notice.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

cards.title: The hot hand fallacy had a fallacy in it
cards.hook: For 33 years the hot hand was the textbook example of humans seeing patterns in noise. Then someone checked the estimator.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Bias holds for n>=3, not every finite n (n=2 is unbiased); the 100-shot claim restated as the ~8pp gap in GVT's three-in-a-row comparison.

cards.title: The 2002 Oakland A's were not smarter. They were shopping in the right aisle.
cards.hook: Moneyball's real claim was never that statistics beat scouts. It was that a skill can be on sale.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Payrolls corrected to sourced figures (A's about $44m, Yankees over $125m) and Lewis's book added as a source.

cards.title: Remember eigenvectors? Sports tables are full of them.
cards.hook: Beating a great team should count more than beating a bad one. Say that carefully and you have written down an eigenvalue problem.
cards.author: author-sports-niche-1

reviewed.notes: Keener 1993 confirmed via Crossref (SIAM Review 35(1):80-93). Removed the unsupported claim that his method ran inside the BCS formula.
